case_title: Kaliya v. State of Madhya Pradesh
high_court_outcome: Maintained conviction of the appellant u/s 302-IPC and acquitted the other accused of the charges
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the mother-in-law of the victim, was involved in an incident where the victim, a married woman, was burnt alive. The victim was admitted to a hospital in a severely burnt condition and recorded a dying declaration stating that her mother-in-law poured kerosene on her and set her on fire. The victim died from burn injuries. The prosecution presented the dying declaration, medical evidence, and witness testimonies to support the case. The trial court convicted the accused of murder, while the High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court reviewed the admissibility of the dying declaration and the evidence presented, ultimately affirming the conviction.
